substack_body_markdown:
U.S. retail sales declined in July, the first drop in nine months, Reuters reported. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

MarketWatch identified cheaper gasoline and an “Amazon Prime hangover” as the chief contributors to the slump. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]] CNN also reported that U.S. consumers cut their retail spending during the month. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_3]]

The available reporting does not specify the percentage or dollar value of the decline, limiting conclusions about its scale.
subtitle: The available reporting points to cheaper gasoline and a post-Prime spending lull, but does not specify the decline’s magnitude.
title: U.S. Retail Sales Post First Decline in Nine Months
